articleTitle: Management consultancy solutions. Development of the project
publicationTitle: IEE Half-Day Colloquium on Management Consultancy Solutions
abstract: The author describes the development of management consultancy projects. Topics discussed include: information preparation; project phases; time requirements; questions to ask; project steering; and results presentation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Half-Day Colloquium on Management Consultancy Solutions
abstract: A consultant is someone, and it is always a person because consultancy is only delivered by a person, who by virtue of training and experience has knowledge which he can impart to or share with others who consult him with a problem. He may proffer advice or he may act more passively as a counsellor, providing an informed and experienced foil to a client sorting out his own problem. There is quite a wide range of services offered in the consultancy market under the heading of management consultancy, by a diverse range of companies and individuals. Here, the author describes some of the advantages and pitfalls of management consultancy.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Half-Day Colloquium on Management Consultancy Solutions
abstract: Today's predominant organisational model has favoured vertical excellence whilst the customer has a horizontal view of the company. Successful organisations have the ability to renew themselves and a major trend is to go from vertical (functional) excellence to horizontal (customer purpose) excellence. In doing so they have to overcome the communication filters in their organisation and find ways of sharing a common message and aligning themselves. As well as the rational content of any change debate there are also the political and emotional aspects which are pre-determinant for the final outcome. Here, the authors describe how management consultancy has significant potential to improve a company's performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Half-Day Colloquium on Management Consultancy Solutions
abstract: The author discusses management consultancy and defines consultancy projects. Topics covered include: problem specification; consultant selection; and consultancy experiences.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
